description: Create an offline pixel-style two-question quiz. #question initially has exact text 2 + 2 = ?. Buttons #answer-a/#answer-b display 4/5 for first question. Clicking one answer locks answers and increments integer-only #score once if correct; score initially 0. #next advances to second question exact 3 + 3 = ?, answer-a is 5 and answer-b is 6. After answering second, #next sets #question to Finished. #restart resets first question and score. Include labels and README. HTML/CSS/JS only, no storage/packages, under 230 lines.

output.goal: Build a client-only pixel-style two-question quiz with score tracking, lockable answers, next/restart flow, accessible labeled controls, and README within 230 lines.

phases.name: Setup and Skeleton
tasks: Create index.html, styles.css, script.js, and README.md file structure
Add semantic HTML elements with IDs question, answer-a, answer-b, score, next, and restart
Link CSS and JS using relative paths
Apply basic pixel-style layout and typography with CSS

phases.name: Core Quiz Logic
tasks: Initialize first question text exactly as 2 + 2 = ? and score as 0
Set first answer buttons to display 4 and 5
Lock answers after a click and increment integer-only score once if correct
Use next button to advance to second question exactly as 3 + 3 = ?
Set second answer buttons to display 5 and 6 with same lock/score behavior

phases.name: Completion and Reset
tasks: After answering second question, set question element to Finished
Implement restart button to reset first question and score to 0
Prevent invalid next or double-answer edge cases
Ensure score stays integer-only and cannot increment more than once per question

phases.name: Accessibility and Documentation
tasks: Add labels or aria-labels to question and answer controls
Ensure keyboard-accessible controls with visible focus states
Write README.md with usage, structure, and offline/no-dependency notes
Verify total implementation is under 230 lines and uses only HTML/CSS/JS

risks: Strict 230-line budget may require compact CSS and JavaScript formatting
Pixel-style visuals must be created using CSS only without external assets
Accessible keyboard controls and labels may add markup length
Answer locking and score state need careful handling to avoid double-click bugs
